dedupe_keys.name: nlr evi roadtrip long distance ev energy use corridor charging station siting and grid load simulation

description: EVI-RoadTrip is a National Laboratory of the Rockies (formerly NREL) tool for high-resolution design and analysis of EV charging networks for road trips and long-distance travel. Contents: it combines road trip volumes and patterns, EV energy use and charging simulation, station siting and sizing, and grid capacity analysis to answer how many charging stations are needed, where, and with what grid impact. It estimates routes, driving conditions, energy use and charging demand for every minute of a trip, and reports station locations (longitude and latitude), facility type such as a gas station or hotel, number of chargers and plug mix, with load profiles for single stations or whole areas. Spatial resolution runs from trip coordinates and 30 m land use to traffic analysis zones, states and the national corridor network; temporal resolution from seconds to years of build-out. Producer: NLR Transportation and Mobility Research, part of EVI-X. Coverage: United States interregional travel along highway corridors. Format and access: NLR software used in analyses; the page gives no public download. Licence: not stated on the NLR page. Caveats: outputs depend on the trip demand data and adoption scenarios supplied. Simulation uses: siting fast-charging along highway corridors, estimating corridor charging loads for utilities, and freight and passenger electrification planning. Related records: platform-nlr-evi-x-ev-charging-infrastructure-modelling-suite and model-nlr-evi-pro-electric-vehicle-infrastructure-projection-tool.
